name: Beid
description: A star 37 parsecs away, 3.4 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 19587: radius 3.422 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 25.536 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.036) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 19587: effective temperature 7019 +/- 133 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.03)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 19587: distance 37.313 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 37 parsecs away, 3.4 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 26 times the Sun's luminosity at 7,019 K, so 3.422 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 19587: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Omicron1 Eridani
quotes.card: Omicron1 Eridani, also named Beid, is a variable star in the constellation of Eridanus.
quotes.introduction: With an average apparent visual magnitude of around 4.0, it is visible to the naked eye on a clear, dark night.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 3196359642878570368 (quality C), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
